name: Replicate
desc: Hosted-API platform for OSS models, part of Cloudflare since 2025-12-01 (still runs as a distinct brand) — Cog format packages models with their environment; thousands of community models behind a single REST API.
deployment: Managed-only — hosted API (Cog is OSS for packaging models)

name: RunPod
desc: GPU-cloud platform — Pods (long-running), Serverless (per-request), and Hub (community templates). Popular for fine-tuning and inference of OSS models.
pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-second or per-hour GPU billing; e.g. H100 PCIe Pod $2.89/hr, H100 SXM Pod $3.99/hr (Secure Cloud), Serverless H100 $4.79/hr; reserved capacity

name: SGLang
desc: Fast LLM serving framework with RadixAttention (cache reuse across requests with shared prefixes) + structured programming primitives. UC Berkeley.

name: TensorRT-LLM
desc: NVIDIA's TensorRT extension for LLM inference — compiles transformers to optimised kernels for Hopper/Blackwell. Used in NIM and downstream deployments.
deployment: Self-hosted only — inference library/runtime for NVIDIA GPUs

name: Text Generation Inference (TGI)
desc: Hugging Face's LLM inference server (continuous batching, FlashAttention, quantization). Entered maintenance mode, then archived 2026-03-21; HF recommends vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp or MLX instead.

name: Together AI
desc: Cloud platform for OSS LLM inference and fine-tuning — serverless inference, dedicated endpoints, fine-tuning API, training cluster.
deployment: Managed-only — serverless and dedicated inference, fine-tuning, GPU clusters
pricing: Serverless pay-per-token (e.g. $0.15–$3.00 per 1M input tokens); dedicated endpoints per GPU-hour (H100 $5.49/hr); fine-tuning per 1M training tokens; GPU clust

name: vLLM
desc: Open-source LLM inference engine with PagedAttention — high-throughput batching, paged KV-cache. UC Berkeley origin; de-facto OSS inference stack.
deployment: Self-hosted only — pip / Docker inference server with OpenAI-compatible API; managed hosting only via third-party clouds

name: 1X Technologies
desc: Norway / US humanoid robot company — Eve (wheeled bimanual) + Neo (legged humanoid, consumer-targeted, late 2025 / 2026 launch). Raised $100M Series B (Jan-2024, EQT + OpenAI Startup Fund); $40M Series A (Mar-2023, OpenAI lead). Distinguishing feature: consumer-home positioning rather than industrial.
pricing: NEO: $20,000 early-access purchase (3-yr warranty) or $499/month subscription; $200 refundable deposit
type: Humanoid robot maker (Neo / Eve) — OpenAI portfolio

name: Agility Robotics
desc: Oregon-based humanoid maker; Digit is in production at GXO Logistics warehouses since Sep-2024 — claimed first humanoid in commercial service in the US. Spinout of Oregon State University. $400M+ raised (Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund participant).
type: Bipedal warehouse robot maker (Digit) — first US humanoid commercial deployment

name: Apptronik
desc: Apollo humanoid maker, spun out of University of Texas Human Centered Robotics Lab. Raised $350M Series A (Feb-2025; B Capital + Capital Factory); Mercedes-Benz manufacturing partner (Mar 2024). Partnered with Google DeepMind on Gemini Robotics (Mar 2025) — Apollo is the headline reference platform for Gemini Robotics.
type: Humanoid robot maker (Apollo) — Google DeepMind partner

name: Collaborative Robotics
desc: Founded 2022 by Brad Porter (ex-Amazon Robotics VP + Scale AI CTO). Stealthier than the humanoid pack; raised $100M Series B Apr-2024 (General Catalyst). Targets warehouse + healthcare collaborative robots.
type: Collaborative robot maker (Brad Porter / ex-Amazon Robotics)

name: Covariant
desc: Pieter Abbeel / Peter Chen-founded robotics FM company — built RFM-1 (Robotics Foundation Model, Mar 2024) for warehouse pick-and-place. In Aug 2024 Amazon took a non-exclusive license to its robotic foundation models and hired founders Abbeel, Chen and Rocky Duan plus research staff; Covariant was not acquired and continued serving customers.
type: Robotics foundation-model company (warehouse pick-and-place) — acqui-hired by Amazon Aug 2024

name: Figure AI
desc: Figure AI — humanoid robot maker founded 2022 by Brett Adcock (ex-Archer Aviation). Figure 02 (Aug 2024) + Helix VLA model (Feb 2025) for full-body / hand control. Raised $675M Series B Feb-2024 (Microsoft / OpenAI / Bezos / Intel; $2.6B val); reported new round at $39.5B val Q2 2025. Partnered with BMW for manufacturing pilots.
type: Humanoid robot maker (Figure 01 / Figure 02 / Helix VLA model)

name: Google DeepMind Gemini Robotics
desc: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics + Gemini Robotics-ER (Embodied Reasoning) released Mar-2025. VLA models built on Gemini 2.0 backbone. Reference platform: Apptronik Apollo. The DeepMind line of robotics-FM, descendant of earlier RT-1 / RT-2 / RT-X work.
deployment: Trusted-tester via partners; Vertex AI / Cloud planned
type: Robotics foundation model from Google DeepMind

name: Hugging Face LeRobot
desc: Hugging Face's open-source robotics platform — datasets, baselines, training code for imitation learning + diffusion policy + ACT. Launched May 2024; growing rapidly with community contributions (HopeJR, SO-100 arms). LeRobot is the de-facto OSS robotics-ML platform analogous to transformers.
pricing: OSS free; HF Hub free + paid tiers
type: OSS robotics platform on HuggingFace (datasets + models + policies)

name: K-Scale Labs
desc: Open-source humanoid robot maker — K-Scale OS (Kos), Stompy and KBot humanoids. YC W24. Pitched as the 'open-source humanoid' alternative to Figure / Tesla — full hardware + software OSS.
license: MIT (kos); K-Bot software GPL-3.0, hardware CERN-OHL-S
type: Open-source humanoid + OS — Y Combinator W24

name: NVIDIA GR00T / Isaac
desc: NVIDIA Project GR00T (Mar-2024) — general-purpose humanoid foundation model + Isaac simulation stack + Jetson Thor compute. GR00T N1 model released open March 2025. NVIDIA's full-stack play: model + sim + compute + training cloud (Cosmos). Major partners include Figure, Apptronik, Boston Dynamics, Agility.
deployment: On-robot (Jetson Thor) + simulation (Isaac Sim) + training cloud (Cosmos)
pricing: OSS weights free; Cosmos / Jetson hardware sold separately
license: Apache-2.0 code; model weights NVIDIA Open Model License

name: OpenMind OM1
desc: OpenMind — open robot OS (OM1) + FABRIC interconnect, founded by Jan Liphardt (Stanford). Pitched as the 'Android of robots': any humanoid + any LLM + the same OS layer. Raised $20M Series A (Pantera + others, 2025).
deployment: Self-hosted only — prebuilt binaries for Linux/macOS or build from source; connects to robot HAL/ROS2 via DDS or websockets
type: Open robot OS / agentic framework (FABRIC + OM1)

name: Physical Intelligence (π)
desc: Founded 2024 by Sergey Levine (UC Berkeley) and Karol Hausman + others (ex-Google Brain Robotics). Building general-purpose robot foundation models (π0 released Oct-2024; π0.5 in 2025) trained on cross-embodiment robot trajectories. Raised $400M Series A (Nov-2024; Jeff Bezos, OpenAI, Thrive, Lux) at $2.4B val.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — openpi weights self-hosted; Pi API beta (managed fine-tuning + hosted inference, waitlist) since 2026-10-13

name: Pickle Robot
desc: MIT spinout focused on truck-unloading robots — autonomously empties truck trailers. Raised $50M Series B (Mar 2024, Tiger Global + others). Narrow focus but production deployments at major logistics customers.

name: Sanctuary AI
desc: Vancouver-based Physical AI company, founded 2018; originally built the Phoenix humanoid, and since 2026-06 deploys hardware-agnostic Physical AI on existing commercial industrial robots (Tier 1 automotive proof-of-concept), with hydraulic hands in development.

name: Toyota Research Institute LBM
desc: Toyota Research Institute's robotics group — published Large Behavior Models (LBMs) Sep-2023 + diffusion-policy / behavior-cloning at scale. Industrial-research lab with Toyota's manufacturing-data advantage. Not a startup — division of Toyota Motor Corp.
deployment: Research-stage; Toyota internal pilots; OSS code for community
type: Robotics research lab — Large Behavior Models (LBM)

name: AWS SageMaker
desc: AWS's managed ML platform — Studio, Training, HyperPod (large-scale clusters), Endpoints. Industry-standard for enterprise AWS-hosted training.
pricing: Pay-as-you-go by instance type and duration, no minimum fees; free tier for new users; savings plans for commitments

name: Accelerate (Hugging Face)
desc: Hugging Face's abstraction over distributed-training backends (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, Megatron). Minimal code change to scale a PyTorch script.
deployment: Self-hosted only — pip-installable Python library (pip install accelerate); runs on local, multi-GPU, TPU and multi-node clusters
pricing: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); no paid tier

name: Argilla
desc: Open-source data-quality platform for LLM training data — human-in-the-loop labelling, RLHF data collection, dataset curation. Acquired by Hugging Face 2024.
deployment: Self-hosted only — server deployed via Hugging Face Spaces template; Python SDK client

name: Axolotl
desc: Open-source LLM fine-tuning library — single YAML config drives full / LoRA / QLoRA / DPO training across most popular base models.
deployment: Self-hosted only — library/CLI with Docker images; runs on third-party GPU clouds

name: Azure Machine Learning
desc: Microsoft Azure's managed ML platform — pipelines, AutoML, Designer, prompt flow (LLM). Heavy integration with Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Studio.
pricing: No additional charge for Azure Machine Learning; pay for underlying compute and other Azure services consumed

name: Bonito
desc: Open model that generates instruction-tuning data conditioned on unstructured text — adapts pretrained LLMs to specialised tasks without manual labels (Brown Univ).
type: Conditional task generator for instruction tuning

name: Cleanba
desc: Distributed PPO/IMPALA reference implementations from CleanRL author — research-friendly, reproducible.

name: ClearML
desc: Open-source ML experiment tracking, orchestration, and data management. Allegro AI commercial; widely used in research labs.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — hosted Community/Pro; VPC or on-prem on Scale/Enterprise; open-source server self-hostable
pricing: Community $0 (up to 3 users); Pro $15/user/mo plus usage; Scale and Enterprise custom quote

name: ColossalAI
desc: HPC-AI Tech's distributed training framework — ZeRO + tensor/pipeline parallel + heterogeneous training (CPU offload). HPC-AI raised $50M.

name: Comet ML
desc: ML experiment tracking + LLM evaluation platform (Opik for LLM eval). Comet competes head-to-head with Weights & Biases.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — Comet cloud; Opik self-hosted via Docker Compose/Helm; on-prem on Enterprise
pricing: Opik: open source free, Free Cloud $0, Pro Cloud $19/mo, Enterprise custom; Experiment Management: Free, Pro $19/user/mo, Enterprise custom
license: proprietary; comet-ml SDK MIT; Opik Apache-2.0

name: Composer (MosaicML)
desc: Open-source training library from MosaicML (Databricks) — Trainer + recipes for fast convergence; underlies the MPT model training stack.

name: DPO
desc: Stanford method that converts RLHF into a supervised-learning loss over preference pairs — no separate reward model needed; widely adopted alignment recipe.

name: DVC
desc: Open-source data and ML model version control — git-like commands for datasets/models stored in cloud blob storage. Created by Iterative.ai; the project was acquired by lakeFS (Treeverse) in Nov 2025 and now lives at github.com/treeverse/dvc.
deployment: Self-hosted only — CLI and VS Code extension

name: Dagster
desc: Data orchestrator with first-class ML pipeline support — software-defined assets model; competes with Airflow/Prefect for ML pipelines.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — Dagster+ Serverless or Hybrid; OSS self-hosted
pricing: Dagster+ Solo $10/mo, Starter $100/mo (plus per-credit and serverless compute usage), Pro custom
